IndustrialArchaeologySurvey06: A Victorian wall box dating from the late 1870s. This is an unusual type, with the collection plate recessed into the door. It is also unusual in retaining an enamelled collection plate, though this is not the original.

A letter box is marked near this site on the 1860s and  the early 20th century Ordnance Survey maps. The present letter box is of a later period and is on a site slightly further to the north away from the junction.
A very graceful curve across the river, with vertical fall of water. One of the more picturesque weirs on the river.
An early letter box, dating from the period 1883-1887
An mid-19th century single-arch bridge of granite. Includes plaques on the parapets, one marking 9½ miles from Dublin, the other inscribed "Kilternan Bridge 1852"
Appears to be granite-flagged ford, just downstream from Shanganagh bridge. This was shown as a ford on an estate map of 1826, just before the bridge was built
